patients.label: Case 1: 55-year-old man, construction worker, with Wallenberg syndrome due to right vertebral artery dissection

identity_evidence.quote: A 55-year-old male construction worker with a long history of smoking and alcohol consumption presented with sudden-onset vertigo, imbalance, headache, and diplopia.

attribution_limitations: Only presentation preceding the examination, workup and treatment is supported; the relative order of examination, laboratory tests, CT, MRI/angio-MRI, cardiac studies and treatment among themselves is not stated.
Early rehabilitation and vascular risk factor management for Case 1 appear only in the abstract statement about both patients; no details, timing or outcome are given.
Discussion text about early vascular imaging and general management recommendations is guideline/literature background, not an additional patient fact.

The abstract describes the CT findings as inconclusive in both cases, while the Case 1 narrative states the non-contrast head CT showed no acute ischemia or hemorrhage; the authors use 'inconclusive' for a CT that did not show the medullary infarct.

patients.label: Case 2: 41-year-old man with Wallenberg syndrome and Factor V Leiden thrombophilia without dissection

identity_evidence.quote: A 41-year-old man without a previous remarkable medical history, particularly head/neck trauma, presented to the emergency department

attribution_limitations: Authors propose, but do not establish, that Factor V Leiden/activated protein C resistance hypercoagulability contributed to the ischemia ("potentially related", "may have contributed"); the etiologic link is a hypothesis.

Case 2 CT is described as inconclusive in the results and as not identifying acute abnormalities (non-contrast) in the discussion of both cases; these are retained together, not reconciled into a normal CT.

Table 1 reference ranges/negativity thresholds are printed by the authors; abnormal/normal flags are not derived from them except where the text states the result (activated protein C resistance, Factor V Leiden positive).
Anticardiolipin IgG/IgM results are printed as a single combined cell; kept as the literal text without assigning values to isotypes.

Only presentation preceding the examination, workup and treatment is supported; the relative order of examination, laboratory tests, CT, MRI/angio-MRI, cardiac studies and treatment among themselves is not stated.
Antiplatelet therapy, statin, BP optimization and DVT prophylaxis are listed as treatment included; agents, doses, routes and durations are not stated.
